key_insight: Physician and nurse use of a clinical LLM assistant is dominated by documentation and knowledge retrieval, but common public benchmarks poorly match that real-world workload.
clinical_relevance: Benchmark scores may overstate readiness for deployment because they do not reflect the tasks clinicians actually send to AI tools in practice.
method: Analyzed 127,833 queries from 6,342 clinicians across 35 specialties during an 8-month rollout.
Used RCQ-Map, a clinician-validated framework, to classify task, intent, answerability, missing information, and potential harm.
Compared real-world query patterns with 58 public benchmarks from major evaluation suites and frontier model reports.
evidence_signal: Documentation and administration accounted for 36.2% of use and knowledge retrieval 28.9%, while the median benchmark had no documentation requests and matched only 31% of the real task mix.
watch_item: Because many benchmarks do not resemble deployment conditions, institutions should be cautious about using benchmark scores alone to decide clinical AI readiness.
paper_title: Clinician use of language models diverges from how the models are evaluated
